---
title: "triage-backlog.yml"
---

Backlog triage that labels and never closes.
The workflow has no schedule of its own: the example stub runs it weekly.
The workflow gives each open issue that has no priority label
the label the triage plan proposes: `P1`, `P2`, or `P3`.
An issue the plan would close, as junk or a duplicate, is left as it is,
for a pass that a person reads.
This implements
[gha#1900](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1900).

The workflow runs the
[`triage-backlog`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/tree/main/triage-backlog)
composite action, which runs `triage-backlog.py` with `--apply --labels-only`.
The script reads issues through the `gh` CLI, so the job checks out nothing.
The action copies the script's summary into the job summary.

## Before the first real run

Create the labels `P1`, `P2`, and `P3` in the repository.
A run that is not a dry run checks for them before it changes anything,
and fails when one is missing.

Run it once by hand as a dry run, and read the plan in the log.

## Inputs

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `dry-run` | boolean | `true` | Print each label command without running it. A scheduled caller passes `false` to label for real. |
| `ceiling` | string | `''` | The open-issue count to report against, as a whole number. Empty means no ceiling. A run over the ceiling still passes, with a warning. |
| `limit` | string | `''` | The most open issues to fetch, as a whole number of 1 or more. Empty means the script's default of 1000. The run fails when the repository has this many open issues or more, because the list may be cut short. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`vars.CI_RUNNER` in a private repository that sets it; otherwise `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

The workflow triages the repository that calls it.
To triage another repository,
call the composite action directly with its `repo` and `github-token` inputs.

## Permissions

Grant `issues: write` on the calling job.
The job declares it whatever `dry-run` is, so a dry run needs the grant too.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/triage-backlog.yml in your repo.
name: Triage backlog

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 14 * * 1' # Mondays, 14:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry-run:
        description: Print each label command without running it.
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  triage:
    permissions:
      issues: write
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/triage-backlog.yml@v3
    with:
      # false on the schedule, the ticked box on a manual run,
      # and true on any other trigger you add.
      dry-run: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && (github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.dry-run) }}
      # ceiling: '400'   # warn when more issues than this are open
      # limit: '2000'    # raise when the repo has 1000 open issues or more
```

See
[`examples/triage-backlog.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/triage-backlog.yml)
for the full caller stub.
